name: Crypto volatility arbitrage
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Mispriced Digital Asset Volatility
caseLead: Differences between implied and realised volatility in Bitcoin and Ether options can create opportunities for hedged volatility strategies. Differences in investor demand and limited arbitrage capacity across exchanges can sustain these gaps, particularly around regulatory decisions and large changes in leveraged positions.
caseRest: A large digital asset price move or exchange failure can overwhelm hedges and prevent positions from being adjusted. Digital asset prices can fall by more than a third in a day, and exchange margin rules or withdrawal restrictions can prevent positions from being adjusted when it matters most. Rehyn estimates that these gaps explain why the largest losses are far bigger than the strategy's typical monthly variation suggests.
figNote: Each card shows the one-day change in the Bitcoin price on the main day of the episode. Bitcoin typically moves by about 2% to 3% in a day, so figures far above that indicate market stress.

events.title: Covid sell-off forces a rush for cash
events.text: A global rush for cash during the Covid sell-off cut Bitcoin by about 37% on 12 March 2020 as leveraged positions were closed. The strategy lost because realised volatility far exceeded implied volatility and exchange margin requirements limited hedging.

events.title: China regulatory warnings hit Bitcoin
events.text: Chinese regulatory warnings on crypto services and the closing of leveraged positions cut Bitcoin by about 14% on 19 May 2021. Results were mixed because the fall caused losses that day, while high implied volatility afterwards allowed options to be sold at rich prices.

events.title: Russia sanctions drive a Bitcoin rebound
events.text: Bitcoin rose about 14% on 28 February 2022 as Russia's invasion of Ukraine and financial sanctions raised interest in assets outside the banking system. Results were mixed because sharp price moves strained hedges, while implied volatility stayed above realised volatility for several weeks.

events.title: FTX collapse spreads through digital asset markets
events.text: The collapse of the FTX exchange in November 2022 cut Bitcoin by about 14% on 9 November and froze funds held on the exchange. The strategy lost because exchange risk, wider spreads and trapped collateral prevented hedges from being adjusted.

events.title: US election result lifts Bitcoin to a record
events.text: The result of the US presidential election on 5 November 2024 lifted Bitcoin about 9% the next day to a record high, on expectations of lighter regulation. The strategy gained because implied volatility had risen into the vote and fell back sharply afterwards.

events.title: US tariff threat on China triggers forced selling
events.text: A threat of extra US tariffs on China on 10 October 2025 cut Bitcoin by about 7% and forced the closing of leveraged positions worth about 19 billion US dollars. The strategy lost because prices on several exchanges moved apart and hedging costs rose.

instrument: Bitcoin and Ether options on major regulated and offshore exchanges; one to four weeks to expiry; hedged with perpetual futures
rules: Options sold when implied volatility exceeds forecast realised volatility and bought when it is below; delta hedged with perpetual futures; exposure capped per exchange; reduced when funding rates or margin requirements rise sharply
costs: Estimated option spreads, exchange fees, funding charges and slippage deducted at each hedge
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from volatility mispricing to exchange risk limits

legs.purpose: Earns premium when implied volatility is high
Owns volatility when it is cheap

legs.instrument: Treasury bills held at regulated custodians
legs.purpose: Provides margin and earns the cash rate

entry: Difference between implied and forecast realised volatility of at least 6 points
size: Set to a 15% annualised volatility target; no more than 25% of margin on one exchange
exit: Closed when the volatility gap falls below 2 points, or 3 days before expiry
stop: All positions closed if Bitcoin moves by more than 12% in one day
marketWatch: The gap between implied and forecast realised volatility in Bitcoin and Ether options is the main indicator for this strategy now, together with funding rates on perpetual futures. Regulatory decisions, scheduled policy announcements and changes in exchange margin rules matter because they can move prices and option demand within hours. Rehyn also watches differences in option prices between exchanges, since wider gaps signal both opportunity and liquidity stress.

favourable.heading: Implied volatility rises into events
favourable.text: Implied volatility that rises ahead of an event favours the strategy because options can be sold at rich prices and hedged efficiently. In January 2024 implied volatility on Bitcoin options rose before the approval of US spot Bitcoin funds and fell after the decision.

favourable.heading: Deeper liquidity on regulated venues
favourable.text: Deeper liquidity on regulated venues favours the strategy because tighter spreads cut hedging costs and make mispricing easier to trade. Rehyn estimates that spreads narrowed as institutional participation grew after the launch of US spot Bitcoin funds in January 2024.

favourable.heading: Policy events with known dates
favourable.text: Scheduled policy events favour the strategy because implied volatility tends to rise before the event and fall once the outcome is known. Selling options into the November 2024 US election, when implied volatility rose before the vote and fell back afterwards, earned premium.

adverse.heading: Sudden closing of leveraged positions
adverse.text: Sudden closing of leveraged positions hurts the strategy because prices move quickly and margin requirements rise at the same time. On 12 March 2020 Bitcoin fell about 37% in one day, which exceeded the range priced by options.

adverse.heading: Exchange failure or frozen withdrawals
adverse.text: The failure of an exchange hurts the strategy because collateral held there can become inaccessible while positions are still open. FTX halted withdrawals in November 2022, and Bitcoin fell about 14% on 9 November.

adverse.heading: Thin liquidity during forced selling
adverse.text: Large moves in thin liquidity hurt the strategy because spreads widen and hedges are executed at worse prices. During the sell-off on 10 October 2025, prices on several exchanges moved apart and hedging costs rose sharply.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, using Bitcoin and Ether option prices and the hedging rules above. Each event window runs from the last strategy high before the shock to the subsequent low, including estimated exchange fees and funding charges.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in Bitcoin and Ether and in implied volatility, which are then applied to the strategy's current option and futures positions.
